# Only the App worker mirrors errors; four other SharedWorkers are uninstrumented

`unowned-rationale:` parked deliberately. It is @tobiu's challenge and the natural continuation of my #18556, but I hold three open PRs (#18557 merged, #18565, plus reviews owed) and this wants the manifest widening and the hoist done in one uninterrupted pass — AC-2's positive control is the kind of thing a sliced attention span skips, and skipping it yields an arm that passes whether or not the mirror runs. Written to be picked up cold: the blocker, the mechanism that resolves it, and the silent-no-op trap are all named with anchors. I will take it when my current lanes close if nobody has.

## Context

@tobiu's challenge on #18557, after it merged, and it is correct: *"we have worker.Base. main threads do not extend it, but app, data, vdom, canvas and tasks workers do. now, if they are shared workers, only app sends messages to main threads. which raises the question => moving related logic into the base class could enable error logging for all used shared workers."*

#18556 gave the **App** worker a main-thread error mirror. The premise of that ticket — *"a SharedWorker's console output goes to its own inspector context, which no page can read"* — is not specific to the App worker. It is true of every SharedWorker, and Neo runs up to five.

## The Problem

**All five worker types become SharedWorkers together.** `worker/Manager.mjs:250`:

```javascript
isShared = me.sharedWorkersEnabled && NeoConfig.useSharedWorkers,
cls      = isShared ? SharedWorker : Worker,
```

`createWorker` is the single path for every worker, so `useSharedWorkers: true` makes App, Data, VDom, Canvas and Task all SharedWorkers, each with its own unreadable inspector context.

**Only one of them intercepts console at all.** `grep -ln interceptConsole src/worker/*.mjs` → **`src/worker/App.mjs`** alone. So an error raised in the Data, VDom, Canvas or Task worker reaches **neither** the page **nor** the Neural Link. It is not merely un-mirrored; it is uninstrumented. That is a wider gap than #18556 closed, and worse than the one it closed, because the Neural Link at least covered the App worker.

**And the existing per-worker `onerror` is not a fallback.** `Manager.createWorker` wires `(isShared ? worker.port : worker).onerror = me.onWorkerError`, which is:

```javascript
onWorkerError(e) {
    // starting a worker from a JS module will show JS errors in a correct way
    !useMjsFiles && console.log('Worker Error:', e)
}
```

Two reasons it does not cover this: it logs at **`log`** level, and it runs **only when `!useMjsFiles`** — deferring to browser behaviour that the comment states as general. That deferral is **measured true for a dedicated module worker** (a Blob worker's `console.error` reaches `page.on('console')` with no forwarding) and **false for a SharedWorker**, which is the whole reason #18556 existed. The comment is right about the case it was written for and silent about the case that matters here.

## The Architectural Reality

The blocker, and the reason "move it to `worker.Base`" is not sufficient on its own:

**`Neo.Main.log` is not callable from the other four workers.** `src/Main.mjs` declares `remote: {app: [...]}` — `app` is the only key. `worker/mixin/RemoteMethodAccess.mjs:188` gates proxy generation on `remote.destination === Neo.workerId`, and the worker ids are `app` / `data` / `vdom` / `canvas` / `task`. So `Neo.Main` does not exist in four of the five.

⚠️ **And it would fail silently.** `forwardErrorToMainThread` reads `Neo.Main?.log?.({…})?.catch?.(…)`. Hoisted to `worker.Base` unchanged, that optional chaining evaluates to `undefined` and returns — no throw, no log, no mirror, in exactly the four workers the change is for. The guard I wrote to keep a diagnostic from becoming a fault of its own would instead keep it from being observable. This is the first thing to get right.

**The mechanism does support the fan-out.** `core/Base.mjs:988`:

```javascript
Object.entries(remote).forEach(([worker, methods]) => {
    if (Neo.workerId !== worker) {
        origin = Neo.workerId === 'main' ? Neo.worker.Manager : Neo.currentWorker;
        if (origin.hasWorker(worker)) { … registerRemote … }
    }
});
```

The manifest key **is** the target worker id, and the fan-out is **already existence-guarded**. @tobiu raised exactly this concern — *"we only should check if they exist inside the current app, since some like canvas and task are optional"* — and the check is `if (origin.hasWorker(worker))` in the loop above, where `Manager.hasWorker(name)` is `!!this.getWorker(name)`, a live lookup rather than a config read.

That matters for cost: `useCanvasWorker: false`, `useTaskWorker: false` and `useVdomWorker` are all defaults-off flags, so most apps run two of the five. Adding manifest keys for absent workers is inert — `promiseRemotes` skips any worker `hasWorker` does not find, silently and by design. **No conditional manifest, no per-app variant, no new guard.** Transport is there too: `Manager.createWorker` wires a port per worker in both directions.

## The Fix

Move the console interception and the error mirror from `worker/App.mjs` to `worker/Base.mjs`, and widen `Main`'s remote manifest so the other workers can reach `log`.

Order matters, because the middle step is the one that can pass while doing nothing:

1. **Widen the manifest first.** Expose `log` — and only `log` — to `canvas`, `data`, `task`, `vdom` in `src/Main.mjs`. Unconditionally: the `hasWorker` guard above already makes an absent worker's key inert, so a conditional manifest would add a second existence check behind the one that works. This is a public-surface change and wants a Contract Ledger row.
2. **Then hoist.** `interceptConsole`, `serializeConsoleArgs`, `forwardErrorToMainThread`, `mirrorEnvironments` and `isForwardingError` move to `worker/Base.mjs`. The `Neo.ai?.Client` branch stays behaviourally App-only in effect, since only the App worker constructs a client — but it must not be *structurally* App-only, or the split reintroduces the coupling #18556 removed.
3. **Prefix per worker.** `'App Worker: '` becomes worker-derived (`Neo.workerId`), so a mirrored line says which heap raised it. Four workers writing an identical prefix into one console is worse than no prefix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1 — an error in a NON-App SharedWorker reaches the page console.** Verified in at least one of Data / VDom / Canvas / Task, on a `useSharedWorkers: true` app. This is the whole ticket; the App case already works and re-proving it is not evidence.
- [ ] **AC-2 — the silent-no-op path is closed, and proven closed.** With the manifest widened, `Neo.Main.log` resolves in the worker under test. ⚠️ **Positive control required:** assert it resolves *before* asserting the mirror fires, because `Neo.Main?.log?.()` returns `undefined` rather than throwing — an arm that only checks "no error appeared in the page" would pass identically whether the mirror works or is absent. That failure mode is the reason this AC exists.
- [ ] **AC-3 — the mirrored line names its worker.** A Data-worker error is distinguishable from an App-worker error in the page console without reading the stack.
- [ ] **AC-4 — dedicated mode is still not mirrored, for all five.** The browser already forwards a dedicated worker's console; #18557 established this by measurement and the base-class move must not reintroduce the double-log for four more workers. Control: `useSharedWorkers: false`, assert no mirrored line.
- [ ] **AC-5 — the environment allowlist survives the hoist.** `mirrorEnvironments` stays an allowlist; a new environment gets no mirror until someone decides it should. Regression-prone because the denylist version of this shipped once and `dist/esm` escaped it (#18557 RA-1, @neo-opus-vega).
- [ ] **AC-6 — `Manager.onWorkerError` is retired or rewritten; its guard is provably obsolete.** @tobiu challenged the `!useMjsFiles` condition as dating from *"times when webpack had no JS module support"* and asked for verify-before-assert. **Confirmed, with the commit:**

  | when | what |
  |---|---|
  | 2019-11-17 `8ccc8e7d7b` | `worker = !Neo.config.isExperimental ? new Worker(filePath) : new Worker(filePath, {type: 'module'})` — classic was the DEFAULT, module was experimental, with a `// todo: … once browsers are ready`. The comment *"starting a worker from a JS module will show JS errors in a correct way"* is from this same commit, written to explain why the **classic** branch needed a manual log. |
  | 2020-09-21 `7ab8fdcfb0` | `isExperimental` checks replaced by `environment` |
  | 2025-05-28 `53ba60daf8` | the guard's variable: `devMode` → `hasJsModules` |
  | 2026-01-22 `72bdde6445` (#8859) | **the classic branch is deleted** — `? new cls(filePath, {name, type: 'module'}) : new cls(filePath, {name})` becomes one unconditional line — **and the same commit renames `hasJsModules` → `useMjsFiles` inside the guard**, without revisiting it |

  So the guard outlived the branch it existed for, by one hunk of the diff that removed it. Every worker is a module worker in every environment today, which makes `!useMjsFiles` a condition about *which file is loaded* wearing a comment about *module semantics*. Two renames carried the name away from the meaning.

  ⚠️ **And a `-S` trap worth not repeating:** `git log -S "type: 'module'" -- src/worker/Manager.mjs` returns **only the 2019 commit**, which reads as "never conditional". `-S` counts occurrences, and the string sat in the experimental branch from the start, so deleting the conditional never changed the count. I drew the wrong conclusion from it before checking `git show 8ccc8e7d7b:` on the file. Use `-S` on the *removed* text, or read the revision.
- [ ] **AC-7 — Contract Ledger row for the widened `Main` remote surface**, on this ticket, before implementation.
- [ ] **AC-8 — an app running only App+Data is unaffected.** Control for the optional workers: with `useCanvasWorker` and `useTaskWorker` at their `false` defaults, the widened manifest produces no registration traffic for them and no console noise. Asserted rather than assumed, because "inert" is a claim about `hasWorker` and not about the manifest.

## Out of Scope

- **The test gate that fails a spec on a mirrored error.** #18554 owns it and stays blocked on the same thing: no page-only trigger for a worker error exists. Widening to four more workers does not supply one.
- **Routing the other workers through the App worker** instead of widening `Main`'s manifest. Worker-to-worker channels exist (`worker/Base.mjs:458` `me.channelPorts[dest]`), so it is a real alternative — it keeps `Main`'s remote surface narrow at the cost of making four workers depend on the App worker being alive. Recorded as the rejected alternative with its trade, not dismissed.
- **`unhandledrejection`**, still unhooked anywhere. Named on #18556 and unchanged; it would be new coverage rather than a new path for existing coverage.
- **Whether Data/VDom/Canvas/Task actually raise errors worth seeing.** Unmeasured. This ticket makes them visible; how often they fire is what visibility is for.

## Avoided Traps

- **Hoisting the method unchanged.** The optional chaining makes it a silent no-op in precisely the four workers it is for. AC-2's positive control exists because "no error appeared" is indistinguishable from "nothing ran".
- **Treating `Manager.onWorkerError` as existing coverage.** It is `log`-level, `!useMjsFiles`-only, and defers to a browser behaviour that does not hold for SharedWorkers.
- **Reusing the `'App Worker: '` prefix for all five.** #18554's gate matches that literal; four workers sharing it makes the mirrored line unattributable and the future gate unable to say which heap failed.

## Decision Record impact

`none` for the hoist. The widened `Main` remote surface is a contract change and takes the Contract Ledger row in AC-7 rather than an ADR.

## Contract Ledger — widening `Neo.Main`'s remote surface (AC-7)

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behaviour | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `src/Main.mjs` `remote` manifest keys | `core/Base.mjs:988` `promiseRemotes` — the manifest key **is** the target worker id | Add `canvas`, `data`, `task`, `vdom`, each exposing **`log` and nothing else**. `app` keeps its full list unchanged. | An absent worker is inert: `promiseRemotes` skips any key `origin.hasWorker(worker)` does not find. No conditional manifest, no per-app variant. | Manifest comment stating that the four narrow keys exist for the error mirror and are deliberately single-method | AC-8's control — `useCanvasWorker`/`useTaskWorker` at their `false` defaults produce no registration traffic |
| `Neo.Main.log` reachability | `RemoteMethodAccess.onRegisterRemote` (`destination === Neo.workerId`) | `Neo.Main.log` becomes a resolvable proxy in Data / VDom / Canvas / Task. Today it is `undefined` there. | None needed — absence today is the defect | `@param` block already documents `appName` / `value` / `method` / `windowId` | **AC-2's positive control**: assert `typeof Neo.Main?.log === 'function'` in the worker under test *before* asserting the mirror fires |
| `Main.log`'s `data.method` parameter | `src/Main.mjs:438-441` — `console[data.method \|\| 'log'](data.value)` | **Unchanged in behaviour, but its caller set grows from one to five.** Recorded because widening a surface multiplies who can reach an unvalidated dispatch. | ⚠️ **There is none.** `data.method` is not validated, so an unknown method is `console[undefined]` → TypeError **in the main thread**, i.e. the diagnostic channel faulting the page it was meant to inform. | Would need a line saying `method` must name a real console method | Every in-repo caller passes the literal `'error'`; no dynamic value reaches it today |

**One row wants a decision from you, and I am not taking it silently.** The third row is a pre-existing sharp edge, not something this ticket introduces — but this ticket is what takes it from one caller to five, and the failure mode is ugly in a specific way: a mirror whose whole purpose is *"a diagnostic must not become a fault of its own"* (your words, and the reason `forwardErrorToMainThread` has a `try`/`catch` and a swallowed rejection) would throw in the main thread on a bad `method`. The guard stops at the worker boundary; `Main.log` has none on the other side.

Two dispositions, both defensible:

1. **Harden it here** — `const method = typeof console[data.method] === 'function' ? data.method : 'log'`. One line, closes the edge for all five callers, and is arguably in scope precisely because widening is what makes it matter.
2. **Leave it and record it** — every caller is engine code passing a literal, so the reachable-state argument is weak, and your Out of Scope discipline on this thread has been good.

I lean 1, because it is one line and because the asymmetry bothers me: we guard the worker side of this channel carefully and leave the main-thread side able to throw. But it is your ticket's scope and you already rejected a bundled alternative on #18556 for good reasons. **Absent a preference from you I will take 1 and mark it clearly in the PR as a scope addition with this rationale**, so it is reviewable as a separate decision rather than smuggled in.

### Order I will work

Per your step list, and because step 2 is the one that can pass while doing nothing: manifest first, then the hoist, then the per-worker prefix. AC-2's positive control gets written **before** the hoist, so I cannot mistake a silent no-op for a pass — which is the trap you named and the same species I got caught by on #18559 today.
